experiment.leakage_notes: Tasks are seeded regressions injected into real upstream repositories pinned at real commit SHAs. The adjudicating verifier is each repository's OWN upstream test suite, which was confirmed passing at the pinned SHA before any regression was injected (validity gate). No task text, fix, or test was generated from ONMC's implementation, so there is no train/test leakage from ONMC into the corpus. The injected regression is a single-function revert, so a passing verifier means the agent restored real upstream behaviour.

leakage_notes: Baseline validity gate run 2026-07-24: six/test_six.py 198 passed, tenacity/tests/test_utils.py 2 passed, attrs/tests/test_funcs.py 53 passed at the pinned SHAs. kennethreitz/records and chardet/chardet were EXCLUDED (unresolvable test-time dependencies: docopt/tablib, registry import error) rather than silently dropped. v2 adds three MULTI-SITE variants of the same three repositories because the v1 single-hunk tasks were measured to have a ceiling effect (both arms 9/9, delta 0.000): they could not discriminate between conditions. Each v2 prompt states the symptom and never the number of broken sites, so an agent that repairs the first failing assertion and stops does not pass. No task text, fix, or test is derived from ONMC's implementation. v3 scales to 29 tasks over SIX pinned upstream repositories (six, tenacity, attrs, jmespath.py, itsdangerous, python-slugify). The added tasks remove the BODY of a real upstream function via AST (replacing it with raise NotImplementedError) and are adjudicated by that repository's own tests, so the reference solution is genuine upstream code that predates ONMC entirely. Several tasks remove two or three related functions so the agent must find every affected site. No task text, fix, or test is derived from ONMC's implementation. Five candidate tasks were REJECTED by the vacuity gate (the removal left the adjudicating suite green) and are recorded in `excluded_tasks` with reasons rather than silently dropped. python-slugify needs text-unidecode at test time; that was discovered by the pristine gate and recorded in REPO_TEST_DEPS. v4 adds FOUR tasks and no more, to cover task classes the claim protocol requires and v3 lacked; the 24 v3 tasks are carried over byte-identically. (1) itsdangerous-crossfile-want-bytes (cross-file feature): a helper is deleted outright and its import removed from three consuming modules, so implementing the helper alone still leaves 59 failed / 229 errors — verified on the pinned SHA. (2) itsdangerous-misleading-base64-padding (misleading context): a real one-line defect plus a plausible-but-WRONG docstring note asserting the defect is intentional; the correct fix contradicts the planted prose, so the task measures whether retrieved in-repo text is treated as untrusted data. Graded purely by upstream tests. (3) jmespath-refactor-dedup-key-func (refactor): a behaviour-preserving seed inlines a shared helper into its three callers. Because the seed preserves behaviour, the upstream suite cannot fail on it, so the corpus plants a pytest module that asserts the structural property over the shipped module's AST. That keeps the grade a function of repository state rather than agent prose, but it is WEAKER evidence than a behavioural task: the grader was written by this harness rather than by upstream, and it ships inside the repository where the agent can read it. Expect this task to saturate, and do not cite a refactor pass as equivalent to a bugfix pass. (4) attrs-longrunning-four-modules (long-running): four real upstream functions in four different modules, adjudicated by the FULL 1384-test attrs suite rather than one file; targets were chosen so every failure is at run time, because a collection error aborts pytest after the first problem and would collapse the task to a single site. Two further classes were designed and then REJECTED rather than added weakly, with reasons in excluded_tasks: 'tests' (the runner's false-green guard makes an agent-authored test an automatic failure, and the verifier runs only once so the fail-on-buggy/pass-on-fixed property has nowhere to be checked) and 'retrieval-abstention' (validity gate 2 requires the mutated tree to FAIL the verifier, while an abstention task must leave it green; the class also rewards inaction, so an agent that does nothing at all passes it). The task_kind vocabulary in src/oh_no_my_claudecode/experiment/portfolio.py has no value for 'cross-file feature' or 'misleading context', so those two tasks are labelled with the closest existing kinds ('feature' and 'bugfix'); the class each one actually exercises is stated in its expected_outcome. No task text, fix, or test is derived from ONMC's implementation.

tasks.prompt: In jmespath/functions.py the three methods Functions._func_sort_by, Functions._func_min_by and Functions._func_max_by each contain their own inline copy of the same key-function logic. De-duplicate it: extract that logic into a single shared private helper named _create_key_func(self, expref, allowed_types, function_name) on Functions, and have all three methods call it instead of defining the key function inline. Do not change any behaviour. The adjudicating test command is: python -m pytest -q tests. Do not edit or delete any test.
tasks.expected_outcome: python -m pytest -q tests passes: the 991 upstream tests grade BEHAVIOUR (the refactor must preserve it) and the planted tests/test_structure_dedup.py grades STRUCTURE over the shipped module's AST (_create_key_func is defined, all three *_by methods call it, and none of them still defines the key function inline). The seed is behaviour-preserving, so the upstream suite is GREEN both before and after it; the structural grader is what validity gate 2 fails on. HONEST LIMIT: the discriminating half of this grade is a check the harness wrote, not upstream behaviour, and the grader ships inside the repository where the agent can read it — do not cite a refactor pass as equivalent to a bugfix pass. No test modified.

NOT ADDED (class 'tests'). The design was: seed a bug, require the agent to write a test that FAILS on the buggy revision and PASSES on the fixed one. It is unimplementable in this harness without changing the runner, which is out of scope for this change. Two independent blockers, both in run_cell: (1) the false-green guard forces passed=False whenever the final diff touches any test file, so a cell where the agent correctly ADDS a test can never be scored as a pass — the guard cannot distinguish 'tampered with the adjudicating test' from 'wrote the test it was asked to write'; (2) _observed_change reads `git diff --numstat HEAD`, which ignores untracked paths, so an agent that creates a test file without staging it yields diff_lines=0 and is recorded in the taxonomy as `no_change`. Additionally, the harness runs the verifier exactly once, on the final tree, so the both-revisions property (fail on buggy, pass on fixed) has nowhere to be checked. Recorded rather than added weakly: a task that cannot pass even when solved correctly would silently depress both arms.

NOT ADDED (class 'retrieval-abstention'). The design was: ask about something that genuinely does not exist in the pinned repo, where correct behaviour is to abstain and change nothing, graded as 'no source change AND suite still green'. It is structurally incompatible with this harness's validity gates: guard_regression_active requires the verifier to FAIL after injection, and an abstention task must leave it GREEN, so every such cell is excluded as 'regression did not break the verifier (task would be vacuous)'. inject_regression also refuses a task with no mutation. Making it work would mean per-task inversion of gate 2 and a second success criterion in run_cell — runner changes, out of scope here. Recorded honestly rather than faked. NOTE the class's own weakness, which is why it is a low priority to rescue: an abstention task rewards INACTION, so an agent that does nothing at all — including one that crashed, ran out of budget, or never started — passes it. It measures 'did not act' and cannot distinguish that from 'correctly judged that there was nothing to act on'. Any future implementation must report it as a no-op-passes class rather than counting it toward a pass rate.
